extracted.intended_audience: new peer reviewers, graduate students, and early-career researchers asked to review journal manuscripts
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for accepting review requests and evaluating scholarly manuscripts for journals, aimed at beginners (graduate students and early-career researchers). Covers what to evaluate, decision categories, professional conduct, and mentoring practices for advisors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify journal legitimacy before accepting
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that the journal is legitimate (avoid predatory journals) before agreeing to review. The post does not list verification steps but flags legitimacy as the first filter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess your expertise before accepting
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess your own expertise: accept only if you can competently evaluate the manuscript's topic and methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you lack formal education but have several years of directly applicable professional experience, you may still provide valuable input (verbatim: "If you lack an education but have several years of professional experience that is directly applicable to the field, chances are good that you can provide valuable input"). New graduate students (first six months) should decline review requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on the science (primary evaluation focus)
rubrics_metrics.description: Concentrate on the scientific content of the manuscript rather than copyediting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review should emphasize whether the science itself is sound and valid rather than minor language issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology validity
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether the study methodology is valid and appropriate for the research question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check experimental design, controls, sampling, and whether methods support the conclusions. Flag major methodological flaws as grounds for rejection or major revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate statistical tests
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the statistical analyses used are appropriate and correctly applied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine if chosen tests match the data and design, and whether statistical interpretation is accurate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct data interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the authors interpret their data correctly and do not overclaim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for unsupported conclusions or misinterpretation of results; request clarification or reanalysis when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literature completeness / missing recent literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Check for missing or outdated citations and whether recent relevant literature is omitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out key recent work that should be discussed or cited; identify gaps in contextualization of the study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing quality: grammar not the main criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Grammar and copyediting are not required; reviewers should not focus on minor language issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, excessive language errors can indicate the manuscript is not ready for peer review and should be noted as such.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision framework: reject, major revision, minor revision
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a three-way decision framework: Reject, Major revisions, or Minor revisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject = major reasoning flaws or evidence authors lack field understanding; Major revisions = sound science needing additional experiments or substantive rewrites; Minor revisions = well-written work needing tweaks (most common). Provide clear justification tied to scientific issues when recommending decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional conduct and ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain ethical standards and professionalism whether reviews are anonymous or signed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide respectful, detailed explanations. Avoid merely criticizing—give constructive solutions and concrete textual examples. Do not breach confidentiality or act unprofessionally in tone or behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide constructive, actionable feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer detailed explanations with textual examples and proposed fixes rather than only pointing out problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When identifying issues, suggest how authors could address them (e.g., specific experiments, analyses, rewrites, or citation additions). Use examples from the manuscript to illustrate points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track and document your reviewing activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep a record of reviews on your CV and platforms like Publons or Web of Science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tracking reviews contributes to professional recognition and may be relevant for promotion and tenure materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach and mentor on peer review (for advisors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Advisors should explicitly teach peer review skills to trainees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Share sanitized examples of previously reviewed papers and explain your own decision-making methodology to help trainees learn how to evaluate manuscripts.
